documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 3:30 follow-up. Called, no answer, left voicemail to rebook. Texted the scheduling link.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked after missing April (sick kid at home that day).
On nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly since August 2021 for the urethral diverticulum. No infections in that time. No dysuria. Occasional small dribble after voiding, unchanged. Takes the capsule with dinner.

Exam: afebrile, BP ok. Abdomen soft, no suprapubic or CVA tenderness.
UA in office: no leukocyte esterase, nitrite negative.

A/P
- Urethral diverticulum, suppressed: continue nitrofurantoin nightly. Refills on file.
- Fibroids: no symptoms.
Physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
36F here for yearly exam. Busy start to the school year; walking the kids to school most mornings.
No UTIs on suppression. Periods regular, not heavy. No pelvic pain.
Meds: nitrofurantoin 100 mg qhs, prenatal vitamin (keeps taking it).
NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals fine. Well appearing. HEENT clear. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, old scars. Skin no concerning lesions. No edema.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Long-term nitrofurantoin: checking CBC and CMP.
- Diverticulum, fibroids, hx gestational HTN and classical cesarean: unchanged.
- Flu and updated COVID next month at a nurse visit.
- Pap due 2025.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts, kidney and liver numbers are all normal. Fine to keep the nightly nitrofurantoin.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza IM L deltoid and 2023-24 COVID vaccine IM R deltoid. Screening questions negative. Tolerated well.

documents.title: Pregnant again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Positive test tonight! Last period started January 10. Since last time was so complicated I want to get going early. What do I do first?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! Let's do a quick video visit Tuesday so I can go over meds and get the OB referral in right away.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her car after school, identity verified.
LMP 1/10/24, about 5.5 weeks. Home test positive x2. Mild nausea, no bleeding or pain.
Fourth pregnancy. Prior: 2017 vaginal; 2019 classical cesarean with gestational HTN; 2022 repeat cesarean at term (polyhydramnios, malpresentation that pregnancy).
On prenatal vitamin and nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly.

A/P
- Early pregnancy with a classical uterine scar: referral to the same women's health group for early dating and planning. Reviewed that her OB will want a scheduled cesarean.
- Aspirin: OB will restart at 12 weeks as last time.
- Continue prenatal vitamin and nitrofurantoin; OB aware.

documents.title: Prenatal intake
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Women's health group — new OB intake
Visit 03/06/2024, 8w0d by LMP 01/10/2024, confirmed on dating scan (single live intrauterine pregnancy).
G4P3: term vaginal birth 2017; classical cesarean 2019 (gestational hypertension); repeat cesarean at term 2022.
Also: uterine fibroids, urethral diverticulum on nitrofurantoin suppression. NKDA.
Prenatal labs sent; blood count normal, urine without protein.
Plan: aspirin 81 mg from 12 weeks given prior gestational hypertension and family history of preeclampsia. Planned cesarean; no labor. Continue prenatal vitamin and nitrofurantoin. Thank you for the referral.

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: Aspirin again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI back on the 81 aspirin as of Wednesday (12 weeks). Scan looked good.

documents.title: RE: Aspirin again
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks, added to your medication list.

conditions.label: Breech presentation at 36 weeks gestation
conditions.note: Frank breech at 28 weeks, current pregnancy

reports.text: Single live intrauterine gestation, frank breech presentation with hips flexed and knees extended. Fetal heart rate 140. Biometry appropriate for 28 weeks. Placenta completely covers the internal cervical os. Uterine leiomyomas again noted.
reports.conclusion: Frank breech. Placenta previa, os completely covered.

documents.title: Prenatal visit, 28 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Women's health group — prenatal update
Visit 07/24/2024, 28w0d. G4P3.

Pregnancy has gone smoothly so far. She mentions being a bit short of breath now and then. No bleeding, no fluid, no contractions.
BP 120/78, HR 88, FHR 140.
Fundal height matches dates. On palpation the presenting part felt like breech.
Prenatal labs all normal; glucose challenge negative for gestational diabetes.
Ultrasound: frank breech. Placenta lies over the internal os — complete previa.

Plan: pelvic rest, no intercourse, call or come in for any bleeding. Given previa plus classical scar she will be delivered by scheduled cesarean in the late preterm window; date to be set. Tdap given. Continue aspirin, prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin.

documents.title: Antepartum admission summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Area hospital — Antepartum unit
Admitted 08/14/2024, discharged 08/16/2024

37-year-old G4P3 at 31w0d with known complete placenta previa came in with an episode of painless bright red vaginal bleeding at home. No contractions. Bleeding slowed on arrival and stopped within a few hours without transfusion. Fetal tracing reactive throughout. Hemoglobin 10.6.
Betamethasone two doses 24 hours apart for fetal lung maturity.
Observed 48 hours with no further bleeding.

Diagnosis: placenta previa with antepartum hemorrhage, preterm.
Discharge: strict pelvic rest, limit activity, return immediately for any bleeding. Home medications unchanged: aspirin 81 mg, prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly.
Follow-up at the women's health group within one week.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I had some bleeding last week from the placenta and stayed two nights. All settled. I'm on rest now and won't be starting the school year. Do you need anything from me?

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me — we got the hospital summary yesterday. Sounds like OB has the plan in hand. Rest up, and send any work forms our way if they need a second signature.

events.reason: Emergency department record and delivery discharge summary

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Area hospital emergency department
Arrival 09/04/2024 06:40

CC: right upper abdominal pain with vomiting.
HPI: 37 y/o G4P3 at 34w0d, known complete placenta previa (bled at 31 weeks), fibroids, urethral diverticulum on nightly nitrofurantoin, prior classical cesarean, gestational hypertension in 2019. Since yesterday morning: steady, severe pain under the right ribs going through to her back, with nausea and several episodes of vomiting. No vaginal bleeding today.
Meds: aspirin 81 mg, prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg qhs. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 160/100, P 98.
Exam: tender in the RUQ, no rebound, no guarding. Reflexes brisk. No ankle swelling. Gravid uterus nontender.
Labs: Hgb 9.8, plt 70K, AST 120, ALT 150, LDH 600, T bili 2.2. Smear with schistocytes. Urine protein 2+.
Fetal monitoring: reactive, no decelerations.

Impression: severe preeclampsia with hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets.
ED course: OB at bedside; magnesium sulfate and IV labetalol started; taken to the operating room by OB.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Area hospital — Maternity unit
Admitted 09/04/2024, discharged 09/08/2024

Presented at 34w0d with severe preeclampsia (HELLP-pattern labs) and a complete placenta previa. Started on magnesium for seizure prophylaxis and IV labetalol for severe-range pressures. Repeat cesarean delivery the same morning; liveborn infant in stable condition, cared for by the pediatric team. Aspirin discontinued.
Postpartum: magnesium continued 24 hours. Pressures settled into the normal range without oral agents. Labs trended back: on 09/08 platelets 162, AST 44, ALT 58.

Discharge diagnoses: severe preeclampsia; complete placenta previa with preterm hemorrhage (resolved with delivery); preterm delivery at 34 weeks by repeat cesarean; history of classical cesarean; uterine leiomyomas; urethral diverticulum.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly.
Instructions: home BP checks twice daily for a week; return for BP 160/110 or higher, headache, vision change, or RUQ pain. Postpartum visit with OB in 1-2 weeks; see PCP for blood pressure and labs.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 13 days after an emergency repeat cesarean at 34 weeks for severe preeclampsia with HELLP-pattern labs (plt 70K, AST/ALT 120/150, LDH 600, schistocytes), in a pregnancy that also had a complete previa with a bleed at 31 weeks. Discharge summary reviewed. Baby is home and doing well.
Home BP log since discharge: all normal, no headaches, no visual symptoms, no RUQ pain. Incision sore but clean. Bleeding lighter.
Meds: prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin qhs. Aspirin stopped at delivery. Not on any BP medicine.

Exam: BP normal in clinic. Well appearing, tired. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, incision healing without redness. No edema. No clonus.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
- Severe preeclampsia, postpartum: resolved clinically. Repeat CBC and CMP today to make sure platelets and liver tests have finished normalizing. Keep home BP checks through this week.
- Previa and breech: resolved with delivery; closed on list. History of preeclampsia added — talked about the higher long-term heart and blood pressure risk after preeclampsia, which we'll watch with yearly BP and lipids.
- Mood: screen fine, knows to reach out.
- Diverticulum on nitrofurantoin: unchanged.
Physical in the spring, Pap due then.

documents.title: Post-hospital labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: platelets and liver tests are back to normal. Hemoglobin is 11.6, still a bit low after the surgery and blood loss, and should keep climbing on your prenatal vitamin with iron. You can stop the twice-daily blood pressure checks after this weekend if they stay where they've been.

documents.title: Vaccines and BP check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In with the baby in a carrier. Flu IM L deltoid, updated COVID IM R deltoid. BP rechecked per PCP request after her preeclampsia: normal. Home readings normal as well; she has stopped logging.
